mainTopic: A disputed bathhouse that one claimant consecrated. The proof from a ספק בכור is rejected, and then the גמרא discusses whether a doubtful animal can be part of מעשר בהמה.
overview: Two people were fighting over a bathhouse, and one of them consecrated it. The רבנן were unsure whether the הקדש took effect, so they stayed away from it and sent the question with רבה to רב חסדא. On the way, in סורא, רב המנונא said the answer is in a משנה about a ספק בכור. He read it to mean that a כהן who grabs the animal keeps it, and a ברייתא forbids shearing or working it even before he grabs it. רבה rejected this, because a בכור becomes holy by itself, which is different from a person's act of הקדש. רב חנניה then brought a ברייתא to support רבה: doubtful animals go into the pen for מעשר בהמה, so they must fully belong to the owner. אביי first answered that the ברייתא could be about nine animals plus the ספק, where tithing works either way. Then he took this back. He proved from a משנה about a counted animal that jumped back into the pen, together with רבא's rule of מנין הראוי, that a doubtful animal cannot be tithed at all.

steps.title: The disputed bathhouse that one claimant consecrated
steps.stepSummary: Two people each claimed a bathhouse. One of them consecrated it, and the רבנן stopped using it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a bathhouse that two people were fighting over. Each one said, 'It is mine.' One of them got up and consecrated it. רב חנניה, רב אושעיא and all the רבנן stayed away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that raises a new question: can a person consecrate something whose ownership is in dispute?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither person had a clear claim to the bathhouse. If the הקדש worked, using the bathhouse would be מעילה, a misuse of holy property. Because the רבנן did not know whether it worked, they played it safe and stayed away.

keyTerms.meaning: A bathhouse
They were arguing or fighting
It is mine
He consecrated it (made it הקדש)
They kept away from it

phrases.english: A bathhouse over which two people were arguing,
this one said: It is mine,

One of them got up and consecrated it.
They kept away from it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new practical case connected to the earlier discussion of seizing disputed property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling is given. The case is presented, and the רבנן act stringently out of doubt.

steps.title: רב אושעיא sends the question to רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא asks רבה to bring the bathhouse question to רב חסדא in כפרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said to רבה: 'When you go to רב חסדא in כפרי, ask him about this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The question is formally sent onward. The גמרא is setting up the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unknown point is clear: does a disputed claimant's הקדש take effect? Since the רבנן present could not settle it, they send it to a greater authority.

keyTerms.meaning: When you go
Before him (to learn from him)
Ask him

phrases.english: And Rav Oshaya said to Rabba:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָזְלַתְּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְכַפְרִי,
phrases.english: When you go before Rav Chisda to Kafrei,
ask him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָזְלַתְּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְכַפְרִי, בְּעִי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story into a formal question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the הקדש of one claimant to a disputed bathhouse take effect, so that using it is forbidden?

steps.title: רב המנונא cites the משנה and ברייתא on a doubtful firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says the answer is in a משנה: in a ספק בכור, the claimant must bring proof, and a ברייתא adds that the animal may not be sheared or worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה came to סורא, רב המנונא told him: 'This is a משנה. With a doubtful firstborn, of a person or of an animal, kosher or non-kosher, whoever wants to take from his fellow must bring proof.' A ברייתא adds: 'They are forbidden to be sheared or worked.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא brings the sources he will use to answer the question. He explains how they prove the point in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה deals with a בכור whose status is uncertain. It says the one taking from the other must prove his claim. The ברייתא adds that even so, the animal is treated as possibly holy, so shearing and working it are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a משנה (the answer is already in a משנה)
Cases where it is uncertain whether something is a firstborn
Whoever takes from his fellow must bring proof
And a ברייתא was taught about it
Shearing and working, which are forbidden with a holy animal

phrases.english: When he came to Sura,
Rav Hamnuna said to him:
It is a Mishnah.
Doubtful firstborns,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד בְּכוֹר אָדָם וְאֶחָד בְּכוֹר בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: whether a human firstborn or an animal firstborn,
whether kosher or non-kosher:
phrases.notes: A non-kosher animal here means a donkey, the only non-kosher animal with a firstborn law.

phrases.english: whoever takes from his fellow must bring proof.
And it was taught about it:
They are forbidden in shearing and in work.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא: מַתְנִיתִין הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the question from a known source.
steps.raayaObject: That the הקדש of the bathhouse takes effect
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about ספק בכורות together with the ברייתא forbidding shearing and work

steps.title: How the firstborn law proves the bathhouse case
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא explains the proof. The משנה shows a כהן who seizes keeps the animal, and the ברייתא forbids using it even when he did not seize it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here the משנה is saying that if a כהן seized the animal, we do not take it from him, because it teaches 'whoever takes from his fellow must bring proof.' And even when he did not seize it, the animal is forbidden in shearing and work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא connects the dots. Holiness applies even without seizing, as long as seizing would have worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'whoever takes must prove' as referring to the owner taking back from the כהן, so the כהן keeps it. Since the כהן could keep it by seizing, the animal is treated as holy even before he seizes it. In the same way, the claimant could have kept the bathhouse by seizing it, so his הקדש works even without seizing.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן seized it by force
We do not take it away from him
And even when he did not seize it

phrases.english: And here, where it says

phrases.aramaic: תְּקָפוֹ כֹּהֵן – אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִיָּדוֹ,
phrases.english: if a priest seized it, we do not take it from his hand,
since it teaches: whoever takes from his fellow must bring proof,
phrases.notes: He reads this as the owner trying to take back from the כהן, so the owner is the one who must prove.

phrases.english: and even when he did not seize it,
they are forbidden in shearing and in work.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּאָמַר תְּקָפוֹ כֹּהֵן אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the cited sources prove the point.
steps.raayaObject: A claim that would succeed if seized gives holiness even without seizing, so the bathhouse הקדש works
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, read as 'a כהן who seized keeps it,' combined with the ברייתא's ban on shearing and work

steps.title: רבה rejects the proof: firstborn holiness comes on its own
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the בכור case is different. Even if a כהן who seizes must give the animal back, a בכור is still forbidden, because its holiness comes by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: 'You are talking about the holiness of a בכור. Really, I can tell you that if a כהן seized it, we take it away from him. Even so, it is forbidden in shearing and work, because holiness that comes by itself is different.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה knocks down רב המנונא's proof by showing that the בכור case does not match the bathhouse case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה reads the משנה the other way: the כהן is the one taking, so he must prove, and seizing does not help him. The ban on shearing and work comes from the fact that a בכור becomes holy by itself at birth, so a doubt about it is a doubt about holiness. A bathhouse becomes holy only through a person's act of הקדש, so no proof can be drawn from a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of a firstborn
Really, I can tell you (I can explain it the other way)
We take it away from him
Holiness that comes by itself, without anyone declaring it
Is different

steps.whatToRemember: רב המנונא tried to learn the bathhouse case from a ספק בכור. רבה rejected this, because a בכור's holiness comes by itself, while a bathhouse needs a person to consecrate it. So the bathhouse question is still not proven from here.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה does not say the ban on shearing and work depends on who holds the animal. He says the opposite: even if the כהן must give it back, the animal stays forbidden, because the holiness of a בכור does not depend on ownership at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important distinction: holiness that comes by itself is treated differently from holiness created by a person's declaration. Proofs cannot be carried from one type to the other.

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:
You are speaking of the holiness of a firstborn!
Really, I can say to you
if a priest seized it, we take it from his hand,
phrases.notes: So in the משנה, the כהן is the one 'taking from his fellow,' and he is the one who must prove.

phrases.english: and even so they are forbidden in shearing and in work,
because holiness that comes by itself is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה: קְדוּשַּׁת בְּכוֹר קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from ספק בכור to the disputed bathhouse. It does not settle the bathhouse question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban on a ספק בכור comes from holiness that arrives by itself, not from the כהן's possible ownership. The משנה can also be read as 'a כהן who seized must return it.'

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to support רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניה quotes a ברייתא: animals that might be a בכור go into the pen to be tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניה said to רבה: There is a ברייתא that supports you. Animals that might be a בכור enter the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנניה brings a ברייתא to back up רבה. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מעשר בהמה, a person brings his young animals into a pen and counts them out one by one, and every tenth one is holy. The ברייתא says even a ספק בכור goes in with the rest. That hints that the owner still counts it as his own animal.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא
That supports you
Doubtful cases (animals that may or may not be a בכור)
Animal pen
To be tithed (for מעשר בהמה)

phrases.english: Rav Chananya said to Rabba:
It is taught in a baraita that supports you:
The doubtful ones enter the pen to be tithed.
phrases.notes: "The doubtful ones" means animals that may or may not be a בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה rejected רב המנונא's proof, רב חנניה offers a source that supports רבה's own view.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's view that a כהן who grabs a ספק בכור must give it back

steps.title: How the ברייתא proves רבה's view
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן could keep a ספק he grabbed, the animal would be partly his, and the owner could not use it to exempt his own animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that when a כהן grabs a ספק בכור we do not take it from him, why does the animal enter the pen? The owner would be exempting his own animals with an animal that belongs to the כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנניה explains the proof. If a ספק בכור could belong to the כהן, the owner should not be allowed to count it in his tithing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה is taken only from your own animals. If a grabbing כהן could keep a ספק בכור, that animal would really be treated as possibly the כהן's, and counting it would let the owner exempt his own animals using a כהן's animal. Since the ברייתא lets it enter the pen, the animal must belong fully to the owner, so a כהן who grabs it has to give it back.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן grabbed it
We do not take it out of his hand
He exempts his own property using a כהן's property

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind

phrases.aramaic: תְּקָפוֹ כֹּהֵן אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִיָּדוֹ,
phrases.english: that if a kohen grabbed it, we do not take it out of his hand,
why do they enter the pen?
It turns out this one exempts his own property
with the property of a kohen!
phrases.notes: In other words, he would be using the כהן's animal to cover his own tithing duty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ תְּקָפוֹ כֹּהֵן אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא quoted in step 6 supports רבה.
steps.raayaObject: A grabbing כהן cannot keep a ספק בכור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that a person cannot exempt his own animals with someone else's animal

steps.title: אביי says the ברייתא is about an owner with only nine animals
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The ברייתא could be talking about nine animals plus the ספק, where tithing works out correctly either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If you rely on this, it does not support the Master. Here we are dealing with someone who has only nine animals plus the ספק. Either way it works. If the ספק belongs to the owner, he is tithing ten animals properly. If it does not, then nine animals are not enough to need tithing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב חנניה's proof. He shows the ברייתא can be read in a way that says nothing about who owns the ספק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה applies only to a group of ten. With nine sure animals plus one ספק, there are two possibilities. If the ספק is not a בכור, there are ten of the owner's animals and the tithing is correct. If it is a בכור, the owner has only nine animals and owes nothing. So no one is exempted using a כהן's animal, and the ברייתא does not prove that the כהן must give back what he grabbed.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrower reading of a source)
Whichever way you look at it
Subject to the obligation
Fit to be tithed

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the ספק is the כהן's. He is saying the ברייתא's case works no matter who owns it, so it proves nothing either way.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
If it is because of this
it does not support the Master,
phrases.notes: "The Master" is a respectful way of referring to רבה.

phrases.english: here, what are we dealing with?

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אֶלָּא תִּשְׁעָה, וְהוּא
phrases.english: For example, where he has only nine, plus it,
phrases.notes: "It" means the ספק בכור, added to the nine sure animals.

phrases.english: since whichever way you look at it:
if it is subject to the obligation,
he is tithing properly.
If it is not subject to the obligation,
nine are not subject to tithing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם הָא לָא תְּסַיְּיעֵיהּ לְמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חנניה's proof by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not רבה's view itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may describe nine animals plus a ספק, where the tithing is valid no matter who owns the ספק

steps.title: אביי takes back his own answer
steps.stepSummary: אביי retracts. A ספק animal cannot be tithed at all, and he brings a משנה about a counted animal that jumped back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי then said: What I said is not correct, because a ספק animal is not fit for tithing. As we learned in a משנה: If one of the animals already counted jumped back in among the uncounted ones, all of them are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects his own previous answer. He brings a משנה showing that a doubtful animal cannot be part of the tithing count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer in step 8 assumed the ספק could count as the tenth animal if it belonged to the owner. Now he says a ספק is never fit for tithing. The משנה about a counted animal jumping back in shows that doubt about an animal's status blocks tithing. So his "nine plus the ספק" reading falls apart, and the question about the ברייתא is open again.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said (taking back an earlier statement)
What I said is not correct
As we learned in a משנה
Jumped
Animals that were already counted
Exempt

phrases.english: Abaye then said:
What I said is not correct,
because a doubtful animal is not fit for tithing,
as we learned in a mishna:
If one of the counted animals jumped in among them,
phrases.notes: "Among them" means among the animals still waiting to be counted in the pen.

phrases.english: all of them are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר אַבָּיֵי לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי knocks down his own rejection from step 8, which brings back the question of how to read the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects אביי's own reading of the ברייתא as nine animals plus the ספק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ספק animal is not fit for tithing, so it cannot complete a group of ten
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in בכורות: קפץ אחד מן המנויין לתוכן כולן פטורין

steps.title: If a doubtful animal could be tithed, the owner should tithe either way
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues from the משנה: if a ספק could be tithed, the owner should tithe the group, because it works out either way. Since the משנה says all are exempt, a ספק cannot be tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think a doubtful animal needs tithing, then let him tithe, since either way it works. If this group is obligated, his tithing is proper. If it is not obligated, the animals are still exempt because they were counted in a count that was fit to reach ten.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the משנה about the counted animal that jumped back proves that a ספק cannot be tithed. If it could be tithed, the משנה should have told the owner to tithe, because nothing could go wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the counted animal mixes back in, every animal coming out is in doubt. If a ספק could be tithed, the owner could safely tithe, because the result is correct whether the group is obligated or not. Since the משנה instead exempts them all, we learn that a ספק animal is simply not tithed.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubtful case, here an animal whose status is uncertain
To tithe
Whichever way you look at it; it works out in both cases
Subject to the obligation, here the obligation of animal tithe

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the owner should tithe. He is saying that if a ספק could be tithed, the משנה would have told him to. The משנה did not, and that is the proof.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that a doubtful animal requires tithing,
let him tithe, whichever way you look at it:
phrases.notes: The משנה ruled that all the animals are exempt. Here אביי asks why it didn't just tell him to tithe.

phrases.english: because if it is subject to the obligation
he is tithing properly,
and if it is not subject to the obligation
it is exempt through a count that was fit to reach ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ סְפֵיקָא בָּעֵי עַשּׂוֹרֵי, לְעַשֵּׂר מִמָּה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the משנה cited in Step 9 proves that a ספק cannot be tithed.
steps.raayaObject: A ספק animal cannot be tithed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה ruling that when a counted animal jumps back into the pen, all the animals are exempt, rather than telling the owner to tithe 'either way'.

steps.title: רבא's rule: a count that could reach ten exempts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source for the 'either way' argument: רבא rules that a count that was fit to reach ten exempts the animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: a count that was fit to reach ten exempts the animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the second half of the 'either way' argument by quoting רבא. A count that started out able to reach ten frees the counted animals, even if ten was never actually reached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this rule, the 'not obligated' side of the argument would fail, because the nine animals might still owe tithe later. רבא's rule closes that gap: they were already exempted by being counted, so tithing would truly work out either way.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose ruling is quoted here
A count that was fit to reach ten
Exempts

steps.whatToRemember: A ספק animal is not tithed. The proof is that the משנה exempts the whole group instead of telling the owner to tithe 'either way', even though רבא's rule of מנין הראוי would have made tithing safe.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is what makes the 'either way' argument airtight, so the משנה's silence about tithing can only mean that a ספק cannot be tithed.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
A count that was fit to reach ten exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the 'not obligated' side of Step 10's 'either way' argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A count that was fit to reach ten exempts the counted animals from animal tithe, even if ten is not completed.
